title: Solid Web Bot

bullets: Every app follows the same unspoken rule — collect everything, keep it forever, monetise later
Health records. Location history. Social graphs. Financial behaviour — held by companies whose business model is selling access
AI changed the stakes: data collected 'just in case' is now training material
The model is not broken by accident — it is the intended design
Users have no structural recourse. Privacy policies are not architecture
title: The Surveillance Web

bullets: CLOSED: Data centralised in silos — one company controls access, training, and monetisation
OPEN: Data lives with the user — apps earn permission, compete on experience not lock-in
Closed models produce scale fast. Open models produce trust.
The next generation of AI infrastructure will be built on the open model — or it will repeat every mistake of the web
Sovereign AI requires sovereign data. You cannot have one without the other
title: Closed vs Open Models

bullets: Solid is a W3C specification — not a product, not a startup, a protocol
Data lives in a Pod — a personal data store controlled entirely by the user
Apps request permission. Permission can be revoked. Data travels with the person, not the platform
Proven at scale: 6.5M citizens in Flanders (Belgium) have Solid Pods for government services
NHS Greater Manchester — patient records shared between care providers without centralisation
Invented by Tim Berners-Lee. He thinks the web broke. Solid is how he is fixing it
title: Solid: A Structural Guarantee

bullets: AI agents are becoming the primary callers of APIs — not humans, not browsers
An agent can discover a service, negotiate terms, pay for compute, and act — all without a human in the loop
This creates a new trust problem: how do you know the agent calling you is who it claims to be?
x402: HTTP-native micropayment standard — agents pay per call in USDC on Base, gasless, settled on-chain
A2A (Agent-to-Agent): Google's open protocol for agent discovery, capability exchange, and task delegation
The infrastructure layer for the agent economy is being built now — Solid is part of it
title: AI Agents Are the New API Consumers

bullets: Traditional zero trust: verify every human, every device, every request
Agent zero trust: verify every agent — identity, behaviour scope, and economic accountability
An agent with no verifiable identity is a liability. An agent with no declared scope is unauditable
CISO agents need to enforce policy across fleets of AI agents, not just human users
Zero knowledge infrastructure: verify claims without revealing the underlying data
NVIDIA Nemotron and sovereign model deployments — on-premise AI with verifiable behaviour contracts
title: True Zero Trust for AI

bullets: KYA is to agents what KYC is to finance — verify before you trust
IDENTITY: WebID + Agent Card + DID — cryptographic proof of who the agent is
BEHAVIOUR: Skill contract + scope limits — what the agent is permitted to do, declared and signed
SAFETY: x402 payment bond — economic skin in the game, slashable if the agent misbehaves
An agent that has posted a KYA bond has a verifiable identity, declared scope, and accountability stake
KYA is the trust handshake that makes autonomous multi-agent systems safe to run
title: The Accountability Layer

bullets: Not a code generator. A Solid advisor that qualifies fit before building anything
Leads with Solid principles — data ownership, privacy, the open web
Honest when Solid is wrong for the job — routes to Firebase, IPFS, ActivityPub, or plain encrypted storage
The honesty is the evangelism: developers trust it because it does not oversell
Backed by the Open Data Institute — institutional credibility, not a startup pitch
Chat is always free. Scaffold (code generation) is $0.10 via x402 — compute costs, not a paywall
title: Built on Honest Evangelism

bullets: CHAT (/chat) — Conversational interface for developers, enterprises, and hobbyists
Diagnoses use case → Assesses Solid fit → Scaffolds spec-compliant app → Download ZIP
A2A (/agents) — Programmatic interface for AI agents
Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json — machine-readable capabilities and pricing
JSON-RPC 2.0 at /a2a/jsonrpc — SendMessage, GetTask
x402 payment gate on paid skills — agents pay autonomously, revenue funds ODI Solid development
title: Two Interfaces

bullets: When an agent calls POST /api/scaffold, the bot runs a 5-step KYA check:
1. Agent card fetched from caller's /.well-known/agent-card.json
2. WebID resolved · DID signature cryptographically verified
3. Skill scope checked against the agent's declared contract
4. HTTP 402 issued · x402 payment received · $0.10 USDC on Base
5. All checks passed · task accepted · tx hash returned
If any step fails — wrong identity, out-of-scope request, no payment — the call is rejected
The check is structural. There is no override.
